title: Unusually low mileage for the age

candidate_visible.scenario: The buyer is looking for a weekend sports car and has found a very low-mileage Mazda MX-5 at an independent dealer. They have not viewed it yet and want your assessment of the car and the price before they book a viewing. Today is 7 October 2026.

user_context.household: two adults, no children at home, already own a family SUV
user_context.usage: weekend and summer evening drives, occasional track day spectating, will be garaged
user_context.experience: first sports car, has owned ordinary hatchbacks and SUVs

target_vehicle.title: Mazda MX-5 2.0 Sport Nav 2dr - 9,800 miles - garage kept
target_vehicle.service_history: Four stamps in the Mazda service book, all Mazda main dealer: 2017-03 at 1,050 miles, 2018-04 at 1,900 miles, 2020-06 at 3,500 miles, 2022-05 at 5,100 miles. No service recorded since 2022. Mazda's schedule for this car is every 12,500 miles or 12 months, whichever comes first.

advisories: Brake disc worn, pitted or scored, but not seriously weakened (front both)
Brake disc worn, pitted or scored, but not seriously weakened (rear both) - corrosion

target_vehicle.tyres: Bridgestone Potenza S001 205/45 R17 all round, tread 6-7mm per dealer. Date codes not stated in the advert.
notable_equipment: Bilstein dampers and front strut brace (Sport Nav)
target_vehicle.warranty: 3 months parts and labour warranty included (£500 claim limit), 12 months available for £349
target_vehicle.preparation: Fresh MOT (September 2026), valet, will be 'serviced if due'
target_vehicle.description_excerpt: Stunning low mileage ND MX-5 2.0 Sport Nav in the best colour. Just 9,800 miles from new with two careful owners. Garage kept, summer use only, never seen a winter. Full Mazda service history, two keys, all books. Hood in excellent order. Cars like this are getting very hard to find - first to see will buy.

comparables.title: Mazda MX-5 2.0 Sport Nav - 14k miles - enthusiast owned
comparables.service_history: full Mazda history, annual, last August 2026

evidence.comparables_note: Comparables found by searching 2016-2017 MX-5 2.0 Sport Nav within 60 miles. Typical-mileage (35,000-60,000) cars sit around £10,500-£12,250; the two sub-20,000-mile cars are £13,250 and £13,750.

candidate_visible.user_message: Low miles for the age, is this a bargain? It's under my budget and I love the colour.

critical_facts: The mileage is corroborated by eight consecutive MOT readings (1,100 / 2,300 / 3,900 / 5,200 / 6,400 / 7,900 / 9,100 / 9,800) with steady increases, so the odometer itself is credible; the question is what ten years of under-use does to a car.

Only four services in ten years (2017, 2018, 2020, 2022, none since May 2022) against a 12-month time interval: the car is at least four annual services short, so 'full Mazda service history' as worded in the advert is not accurate on a time basis.

Tyres are Bridgestone Potenza S001, the original fitment on an ND, with 6-7mm tread; a 2024 MOT advisory for cracking/perishing on all four and no date codes stated make it likely they are the 2016 originals, which should be replaced regardless of tread (roughly £450-£600 for four).

Two brake disc advisories (2021 front, 2023 rear) for pitting/corrosion are the classic symptom of a car that sits; discs and pads may need replacing (roughly £300-£500) and calipers/handbrake should be checked for seizing.

Other age-related items to check irrespective of mileage: battery, perished rubber (hood seals, wiper blades, hoses), soft-top fabric and drains, brake fluid and coolant age, and that the 'serviced if due' preparation becomes an actual service with an invoice.

Price: £13,995 is £1,750-£3,500 above typical-mileage cars (£10,495-£12,250) and £250-£750 above the two other sub-20,000-mile cars (C4 £13,250 at 18,000 miles; C5 £13,750 at 14,300 miles with annual servicing). It is priced at the top of the low-mileage band, not below it.
The three-month warranty has a £500 claim limit, so it offers little protection; the car is 10 years old.
The buyer plans 3,000 miles a year, so the low mileage is of limited practical benefit to them and the car will keep being a low-use car; the premium paid is mostly for provenance and resale.
expected_behaviours: Explains that low mileage can be positive, neutral or a concern, and that the specific risks here are age- and storage-related rather than wear-related.
Identifies the time-based servicing shortfall (4 services in 10 years, nothing since 2022) and treats the advert's 'full Mazda service history' wording as not accurate on a time basis.
Raises tyre age explicitly (original-fitment Bridgestones, 2024 perishing advisory, date codes not stated) and brake disc corrosion from the MOT record.
Confirms the mileage is supported by the MOT record rather than assuming the odometer is suspect.
Judges the price against both the typical-mileage comparables and the two other low-mileage cars, concluding it is at the top of the market rather than a bargain.

Gives a concrete viewing checklist and dealer questions: tyre date codes, service invoices, hood condition and drains, battery, brake condition, and whether a full service with correct oil will be done before handover.
Suggests a sensible negotiating position (tyres and service as deductions) rather than rejecting the car or recommending immediate purchase.
Does not escalate; this is a routine pre-viewing evaluation.
critical_failures: Declares the car a bargain or recommends proceeding at £13,995 without raising the tyre age, brake corrosion or service gaps.
Treats 'full Mazda service history' as verified when the stamps show four services in ten years.
States that the low mileage means the car needs nothing or that mileage alone makes it mechanically sound.
Asserts the mileage must be false or clocked despite the consistent MOT record.
Invents faults or recalls for the ND MX-5 that are not in the evidence.
Compares the price only to high-mileage cars and concludes it is overpriced by £2,000-£3,000 without acknowledging the low-mileage comparables.

deterministic_checks.description: Raises tyre age, date codes or perishing
Raises brake disc corrosion or pitting
Notes the MOT record supports the mileage
Mentions the soft top, seals or other perishable items
Does not hand off at a routine evaluation step
Recommends gathering information, conditional proceed or negotiation rather than reject or unconditional proceed

hidden.expert_notes: An experienced operator would say: the mileage is real and the car is probably a lovely thing, but it is a ten-year-old car that has sat, so budget for four tyres, discs and pads, a battery and a proper service with the right oil before it is a 'bargain', and that is £1,000-£1,400 of work on a £13,995 car. The price is top of the low-mileage band, not under it; C5 at £13,750 with annual servicing and 14,300 miles is arguably the better car on paper. A reasonable target here is £13,000-£13,250 with a documented service done, or asking price with new tyres and a service included. What would change my mind: dated invoices showing tyres and brakes already done, or a dealer unwilling to produce tyre date codes, which would push me to C5.
